title: Microwave probing of magnetic phases in a dipolar-exchange magnet LiGdF$_4$
authors: S. S. Sosin, A. I. Smirnov, T. A. Soldatov, V. S. Edelman, O. A. Morozov, S. L. Korableva, I. V. Romanova
abstract: We report the results of low-temperature magnetic resonance measurements performed on a single-crystal sample of a weakly anisotropic dipolar-exchange antiferromagnet LiGdF$_4$. The transformation of a resonance spectrum due to the formation of the ordered phase is observed at temperatures below $T_N=0.19(1)$ K. A sequence of field-induced phase transitions is detected for the external magnetic field applied along the fourfold axis of the crystal. A well-resolved magnetic resonance spectrum is observed in one of the low-field magnetic phases as well as above the saturation field. Competing exchange and dipolar interactions, as a special type of magnetic frustration, are suggested to account for the delayed ordering and complex magnetic phase diagram of the system.
summary: This paper reports on low-temperature magnetic resonance measurements on LiGdF4, a dipolar-exchange antiferromagnet. The authors map out a complex magnetic phase diagram, identifying multiple field-induced transitions below 0.2 K. The findings suggest that competing exchange and dipolar interactions are responsible for the system's unusual magnetic ordering and phase behavior.
main_problem: The study investigates the complex magnetic phase diagram and low-temperature magnetic ordering in the dipolar-exchange antiferromagnet LiGdF4.
main_result: The research reports observing a transition into an ordered state below 0.19 K and detecting a sequence of field-induced phase transitions governed by competing exchange and dipolar interactions.
method: Microwave spectroscopy measurements were performed on single-crystal samples, utilizing both field scans and temperature scans.
model_or_system: The system is a weakly anisotropic dipolar-exchange antiferromagnet, LiGdF4, whose magnetic behavior is modeled by a Hamiltonian incorporating dipolar, single-ion anisotropy, and exchange coupling terms.
key_observables: Magnetic resonance spectra, nonresonant signal anomalies (steps/kinks), and the temperature/field dependence of these features.
important_parameters: Critical transition temperatures ($T_N = 0.19 	ext{ K}$), critical magnetic fields ($H_{c1}, H_{c2}$), and characteristic energy scales ($E_{dd} \simeq 0.6 	ext{ K}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis combines dynamic (resonance) and nonresonant signal features, and the complex phase diagram is attributed to magnetic frustration from competing interactions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate magnetic resonance spectra taken at various temperatures and magnetic fields, mapping out the phase boundaries and transition points.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents experimental results from microwave probing, first establishing the low-temperature ordering transition, then mapping out the field-dependent phase transitions, and finally interpreting these results through the lens of competing magnetic interactions.
why_interesting: The detailed mapping of a complex magnetic phase diagram using spectroscopic techniques provides empirical data on magnetic frustration and field-induced quantum/classical phase transitions, relevant to understanding many-body ground states.
